messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: p-values from GAM
parts:
Rikke:

Your finding of low P-values in a fitted gam for many of your covariates
is not that terribly surprising. It is likely the case that all of
those factors may contribute to where cetaceans are located. You will
still need to go through a model selection process (using GCV scores)
however to identify the most parsimonious model for your data.

We have not fully implemented all error distributions in the density
surface modelling engine. If you wish to investigate other
distributions such as the negative binomial, you might be best to work
with the DSM R package inside R. To learn more about using the negative
binomial in conjunction with fitting a gam, load the mgcv package in R
[library(mgcv)], then request help about the negbin argument to gam
[?negbin]

However, the use of negbin is untested in Distance 6.
